pack.risks: unvalidated idea; tiny DEMO risk only

concerns: Falsification criteria text is incomplete ('mean counterfactu...'); the hypothesis lacks a numeric threshold, minimum sample size, and statistical power plan

Selection bias: the rejected population is non-random and rejected for cause; counterfactual fills on stale quotes are optimistically biased upward and must be treated as an upper bound, never as standalone justification for relaxing the validated-state gate later
Mechanism mismatch: this change cannot improve throughput in its own cycle; claiming so misframes what success looks like
Lookahead risk in offline replay: features must be reconstructed from point-in-time snapshots captured at rejection time, never recomputed from later data
Logging in the firehose hot path could alter runtime timing/behavior; the gate must be bit-for-bit unchanged whether the audit is enabled or disabled
Champion drift: replaying against 'the current champion' is ambiguous across a multi-session cycle; results must pin a specific champion artifact
No explicit commitment to ExperimentRegistry recording, which is mandatory under repo rules
votes.reason: The core design is sound and safe: a strictly observational counterfactual rejection audit (log rejected candidate states, offline-replay through the pinned champion, cost realistically, benchmark against admitted trades in the same sessions) involves no order path changes, no gate modification, and no live exposure, so it clears all MT5/research safety rules. However, the proposal has material defects: the falsifiable hypothesis is truncated mid-statement, the declared mechanism ('improve exploration/validation throughput') mismatches what the change actually does (an audit produces evidence, not throughput), and the methodology as written would systematically overstate rejected-trade EV because states rejected for cause (stale quotes, unvalidated features) have exactly the prices/features the gate deemed untrustworthy - naive replay assumes fills at prices that may not have been executable.
requested_revisions: Complete the falsifiable hypothesis with an explicit numeric criterion (e.g., rejected-population mean counterfactual net EV minus admitted-population realized net EV > X with N >= M samples and bootstrap CI excluding zero)

Add a conservative execution model: exclude stale-quote rejections from the fillable set (or price them with a wide uncertainty band) and report rejection-reason strata separately; label all counterfactual EV as an upper bound
Pin the champion artifact (hash of intel/intelligent_champion.json content) at audit start and attribute all replay results to that hash
Guarantee observational purity: async bounded logging, zero writes to gate/order/config paths, plus a test asserting identical gate decisions with the audit on vs off
Reframe expected_mechanism as 'produce calibrated evidence about gate strictness for a future proposal'; explicitly state this audit cannot authorize gate relaxation

Register the experiment in ExperimentRegistry before the cycle starts and define benchmark comparability: same sessions, identical spread/slippage assumptions, paired per-session comparison of both populations

concerns: Replay timing, entry/exit assumptions, spread/slippage model, and treatment of unavailable/stale quotes are unspecified.
The proposed affected paths could include runtime code; collection and replay must remain strictly read-only and must never submit or alter broker orders.
Comparison to admitted trades needs session, symbol, direction, and opportunity-set matching to avoid selection bias.
Rejected states must be immutable, timestamped records with feature/quote validation reasons and versioned champion/config identifiers.
votes.reason: A read-only counterfactual audit is compatible with DEMO safety, but the proposal is truncated and lacks a precise, reproducible replay specification needed to prevent lookahead and fabricated expectancy.
requested_revisions: Provide the complete hypothesis and explicit pass/fail thresholds, minimum sample size, and confidence methodology.
Specify a timestamp-causal replay protocol: only data available at each rejected-state timestamp, no label leakage, realistic cost model identical to the runner, and deterministic entry/exit rules.
State that instrumentation is observational only, cannot change validation decisions, risk, champion selection, or execution, and cannot call MT5 order APIs.
Define a versioned schema and retention/redaction policy for rejected-state logs, including rejection reason, quote age, feature-state status, champion hash, and execution-cost assumptions.
Add tests for no execution side effects, causal replay/no-lookahead, correct rejection-reason capture, and OOS reporting; register the experiment before running it.

concerns: The proposed change text and falsifiable hypothesis are truncated.
Counterfactual replay methodology, data schema, and cost assumptions are unspecified.
No explicit guarantee that rejected states remain read-only and cannot reach mt5.order_send().
Tests are too broad; required assertions and baseline comparisons are not defined.
The falsification criterion does not clearly distinguish rejected-population results from admitted-trade results.
votes.reason: The audit is safety-compatible and does not appear to affect champion promotion or broker execution, but the proposal is incomplete and lacks sufficient implementation and evaluation detail for approval.
